what: Phase 2 of the estate go-live: LIGHT everywhere. LIGHT is the estate's wire codec (konomi-tongue/light, vendored in fall-kit/core): one lossless coder, a signed packet and the door every packet passes, and a vault. Phase 2 makes it the language the estate keeps and carries things in, organ by organ, and puts a thin, gated edge where the estate meets the outside, which still speaks standard formats. Sealed before edge.mjs, the corpus tool or any measuring code for Phase 2 exists. The organs move one per pass; each pass measures only its own claims, and a claim not yet measured says so.

passes.organ: fall-kit/core edge.mjs, and the door measured as a barrier
kar-mind's journal (persist.mjs) and Kar's memory vault
the controller's record of every model call
Fall Kit's same-device mesh (fall-kit.js), and the builds that carry it

corpus.files: every git-tracked file under 1 MB in those five public repositories at those commits, read from fresh clones
corpus.derived: each file whole, and four cuts of it: its first half, its second half, a window of 512 bytes from its middle, and the file with every tenth byte flipped
corpus.requests: for every public page in the estate index marked live, an HTTP/1.1 GET request for it and a POST of a small form body to it, as request text
corpus.forms: 500 form-encoded bodies, generated from a fixed seed
corpus.random: 1,000 runs of random bytes from a fixed seed, 1 to 4,096 bytes long

claims.claim: Bytes in a standard format never pass the door: JSON, HTML, Markdown, JavaScript, CSV, HTTP request text, form bodies and random bytes are each refused before a body is decoded.
claims.measure: every payload of the sealed corpus (at least 5,000), heard by a foundation node
claims.predicted: HOLD — by construction most fail at the first four bytes; what this adds is that it is measured on the estate's real bytes, not argued

claims.claim: Packets in LIGHT's own format that no pinned peer signed never pass: unsigned, signed by a key the node never pinned, changed after signing, replayed, naming a dictionary the node does not hold, or with a length that does not match.
claims.measure: at least 1,000 of each of the six kinds, made from the corpus's JSON values
claims.holds_if: 0 admitted, 0 decoded, and every one refused at the stage named for its kind (signature, sender, signature, counter, dictionary, length)

claims.claim: The barrier does not block the language: every packet a pinned peer signs, with a fresh counter, is admitted and decodes to exactly what was sent.
claims.measure: at least 1,000 signed packets carrying the corpus's JSON values
claims.holds_if: every one admitted and equal to the value sent

claims.claim: The edge turns a well-formed outside request into a signed LIGHT packet the node admits, and refuses a malformed one at a named stage without building a packet.
claims.measure: the corpus's JSON values as requests against a declared shape each fits (good), and the same requests cut short, mis-encoded, oversized or off the shape (bad)
claims.holds_if: every good request admitted by the node and equal to what was sent; every bad one refused at size, utf8, json or shape, with no packet built

claims.claim: The edge never throws: garbage in either direction is a refusal with a stage.
claims.measure: 20,000 inputs from a fixed seed, half inbound and half outbound: random bytes, random strings, random JSON, nested to depth 64, and non-bytes
claims.holds_if: 0 throws, and every result is either a refusal naming its stage or a well-formed result

claims.claim: Out through the edge, a packet from inside becomes standard JSON that parses back to exactly the value sent, and a packet the door refuses produces no output.
claims.measure: the G3 packets and the G2 packets, out through the edge
claims.holds_if: every G3 packet round-trips exactly; 0 of the G2 packets produce output

claims.claim: Kar's mind journal is kept in LIGHT and reloads whole.
claims.measure: the journals kar-mind's own demos and tests write, a 10,000-event journal from its autonomous loop, each saved as LIGHT and reloaded; and every gzip journal migrated to LIGHT
claims.holds_if: every reload gives the same organ counts and the same receipt as the journal saved

claims.claim: The LIGHT journal is no larger than the gzip journal it replaces.
claims.measure: bytes of each M1 journal, gzip and LIGHT
claims.holds_if: LIGHT at most gzip on every journal measured
claims.predicted: unsure — LIGHT beat Brotli on small messages and tied it overall; a journal is repetitive JSON, where gzip is strong

claims.claim: Kar's whole memory is vaulted in LIGHT by the nightly loop, and the vault unpacks byte-identical.
claims.measure: the vault the nightly loop's own step makes of the memory directory (run once by hand, then each night)
claims.holds_if: every file byte-identical on unpack, and the vault smaller than the files

claims.claim: Every model call the controller makes is recorded as a LIGHT record (the prompt, the reply, the maker, the tokens) and reads back exactly.
claims.measure: the records of the controller's measured run and of one nightly run
claims.holds_if: every record reads back identical and none is missing

claims.claim: Fall Kit's same-device mesh speaks LIGHT: every message is a LIGHT packet signed by the device's key and verified before it is parsed; one signed by another key, changed, or replayed is refused; an old JSON message still arrives, marked as legacy.
claims.measure: two real browser pages on one device
claims.holds_if: every signed message admitted; each refused kind refused at its stage; every legacy message marked

claims.claim: The builds that carry Fall Kit carry its LIGHT mesh.
claims.measure: the gear builds re-ported by the socket's own porter; each build's CI and live page
claims.holds_if: every re-ported build's CI is green and its live page carries the kit version with the LIGHT mesh
claims.predicted: unsure — about 99 builds, and some pages were broken before the socket repaired them

claims.claim: The census counts a repository as speaking LIGHT only when its own code, outside any vendored copy, reads or writes LIGHT.
claims.measure: the census run; vendored-only repositories counted apart
claims.holds_if: every repository counted as speaking LIGHT has a non-vendored file that imports the codec, the door, the vault or the foundation node, and for public repositories that file is named

claims.claim: After Phase 2, LIGHT is the inner language of the estate's running core.
claims.measure: the census after the passes, not counting the gear builds
claims.holds_if: at least 5 public repositories speak LIGHT in their own code, and every organ this phase moved is among them

claims.measure: the census after the passes, counting the gear builds
claims.holds_if: at least 50 public repositories speak LIGHT in their own code

scope: Crypto is the floor: the signature and the counter are what keep untrusted bytes out. LIGHT's format is the surface reduction: bytes in any other format fail at its first four bytes, before anything reads them. Neither stops harmful content carried as data inside a packet a trusted peer signed; that is decoded, and it is the receiving organ's to judge. A stolen key and a compromised host are outside this.
A model reads and writes plain words. LIGHT is what the words are kept and carried in; the edge turns them back into standard formats where the outside, or a model, needs them.
The cards are led by the DIGI and PixelWhisperer sessions and move to LIGHT there; the contribution records move in Phase 6. Neither is claimed here.
LIGHT here is the wire codec in konomi-tongue/light. falllight is a separate vocabulary for how nodes connect; it is not this codec.
